sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Zuo Shang, The True Long is a story - final boss encounter in Mount Soulrend & endgame, found at Peak of Mount Soulrend. Beating it yields Aureate.

Not confirmed post-launch. Phantom Blade Zero does not run an elemental damage system, so there is no weakness table to fill in - nothing here is estimated from how a boss looks, which is exactly how wrong weakness tables get written.

What the game does have is a colour language on enemy attacks, and it is the single most useful thing to learn: a red flash marks an unblockable attack that must be dodged, a blue flash marks a parryable one that should be deflected, and a purple flash means the boss has just parried you and a counter is coming. See the combat system for how Sha-Chi feeds into this.

sections.title: How to Beat the Zuo Shang, The True Long
sections.content:
The true-ending final boss is a two-phase exam on everything the game has taught. Phase 1 is readable: he telegraphs, and the back-turned stance is a trap rather than an opening. Phase 2 removes the luxury of forcing damage - his poise is high enough that reckless combos get punished, so the fight becomes block, parry, evade until the Sha-Chi bar breaks, then a single committed burst.

The build that makes it tractable is a freeze into burst swap: Whiteshadow to chill and slow him, Blazing Edge for the damage window once he is frozen or guard-broken, with You Loong's Deluge available to knock him down when the pressure needs resetting.

Attacks worth knowing

AttackWhat it doesAnswer
Sword BarrageA swarm of swords fills the arenaSpam dodge - do not try to parry it
Gathering WindsRed flash while wind and leaves gatherUnblockable - dodge after the flash
Ephemeral SwordsFive swords fire in sequence, then a leapParry the sword swing, dodge the grab that follows
Ephemeral SpearsFour spears, then a dashUnblockable thrust - dodge sideways, not back
Back-turned stanceHe faces away from youExpect a spinning projectile or a counter-parry - hold your swing

What works

  • High burst damage is the answer: chill him with Whiteshadow, then swap to Blazing Edge once he is guard-broken or frozen.
  • You Loong's Deluge staggers him flat, which is the most reliable way to control the pace of the fight.
  • In phase 1, when he turns his back he is either throwing a spinning sword or setting a counter-parry - do not swing blindly.
  • Phase 2 is a defensive fight: block and parry the melee, evade the projectiles, and wait for the Sha-Chi break instead of forcing damage.
